summary: Western Lane FPA site 24 miles ENE of Florence, Oregon: a 1942 pole tower, a 30-foot tower from 1951-52, and a 1963 three-story cab after the 1962 storm; removed in 1969.

facts.design: Enclosed three-story lookout house built in 1963, after a 30-foot live-in tower was destroyed in 1962
facts.status_note: Removed in 1969 per the register and the Rex page; firelookout.com says destroyed. No source describes standing remains.

events.note: 35-foot pole tower with a 6x6-foot cab (register, firelookout.com); the Rex page gives 55 feet
Rex page quotes a 1951 state report: a 14x14 lookout house on a 30-foot tower. The register and firelookout.com date the 30-foot live-in tower to 1952
The 30-foot tower was destroyed in the October 12, 1962 Columbus Day storm
Enclosed three-story lookout house built the year after the storm. The 1963 report quoted on the Rex page calls the lookout Walker Peak Lookout
Three-story cab removed (register, Rex page); firelookout.com says destroyed
Long-unused site reactivated for the Forest Watch camera detection system (Rex page)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com give 35 ft for the 1942 tower; the Rex page gives 55 ft. The story gives both. The record's height_m of 16.8 matches only the 55-ft figure, so facts omit height.
Rex page quotes a 1951 report for the 30-foot tower; the register and firelookout.com say 1952. The story reports both.
Register gives 2,343 ft (714 m); firelookout.com gives 438 ft. Record keeps the register figure; the story gives no elevation.
The 1963 report quoted on the Rex page calls the rebuilt lookout Walker Peak Lookout. The story reports the quote and does not link it to the Multnomah County Walker Peak record.

sources.title: Walker Point Lookout Site (Western Lane FPA)

notes_for_editor: The 1942, 1962 and 1969 dates agree across all three pages. Height, the 1951/1952 replacement year, elevation and the 'Walker Peak Lookout' name conflict; the record's height_m 16.8 is the Rex page's 55-ft figure and is left for editor decision. Today: only the 2014 reactivation item. The Rex page quotes the 1963 and 1951 state annual reports second-hand. Record kind three_story fits the 1963 cab.
